`Claim:` session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8193-objectview-canonical-groupbyfield`

PM dispatch (objectui PM loop). Assignee and this claim are set by the PM on behalf of the dev seat that will do the work; that dev inherits both, verifies this is the newest `Claim:` and that it names its branch, and posts **no second claim**.

**Hot-file serial cleared.** This card was held until #8188 landed, since both touch `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx`. #8188 landed as `d80447d4e`, so the file is free. Nothing else in flight touches it — #7772 is in `views/metadata-admin/previews/`, #8181 in `views/studio-design/`, #8205 in `providers/`.

⭐ This card is unusually well-bounded and its author was scrupulous about the difference between what it measured and what it did not. Two things to carry:

**The precedent is in-tree and explains itself.** `InterfaceListPage.tsx:157` (`defaultKanbanFromObject`) already migrated and left the reasoning in a comment — *"that read-site now prefers the spec key, so one key is enough."* The `ObjectView` twin twelve hundred lines away was simply not carried along. So this is following an established migration, ⛔ not deciding a new one.

⚠️ **The `groupBy` half is explicitly UNMEASURED and is yours to settle first.** The same expression also writes a view-level `groupBy`. The card says plainly: *"I did NOT measure whether `@objectstack/spec`'s own kanban config declares `groupBy` — check that before deciding whether the `groupBy` half is a second alias to fold or a legitimate key."*

⇒ Measure it at runtime against the spec, with a control that fires (the shape #8171 uses: a `safeParse` that accepts the key paired with the same strict schema refusing a bogus key by name). If `groupBy` turns out to be a second alias, ⛔ **do not fold it in this PR** — report it and file it. One atomic producer site per card is what makes this one reviewable.

⛔ The alias **READS** are off-limits — `ListView.tsx:1536/:1890/:2165/:2494/:2495` and plugin-view `ObjectView.tsx:1283/:1313/:1323`. Stored metadata still authors the alias, and `ListView` already prefers the canonical key, which is the whole reason the sibling could drop it.
